clientsExcluded: CalDAV and CardDAV client apps on phones, tablets, and desktops (for example Apple Calendar, DAVx5, Thunderbird)
Device or vendor cloud backups configured within those client apps

evidence.claim: The MOS package projects only RADICALE_ADMIN_USERNAME and RADICALE_ADMIN_PASSWORD into the service and mounts one local data volume; it sets no analytics, update-check, external-service, or telemetry variables.

The package entrypoint configures htpasswd authentication with bcrypt against a local /data/users file and creates the bootstrap user and a default calendar collection on the local data volume; no upstream account or service is contacted during provisioning.

Radicale 3.7.1 is a self-hosted CalDAV/CardDAV server that serves DAV over its own port and stores collections on the local filesystem; its documentation describes no telemetry, usage analytics, update check, or phone-home behaviour.

The packaged tomsquest/docker-radicale image wraps upstream Radicale with a local container healthcheck and optional local brute-force protection; it does not add an outbound analytics, licensing, or update service.
All calendar and contact data is persisted to the single data:/data package volume, so CalDAV/CardDAV collections stay within the MOS runtime rather than any upstream store.

telemetryControls.claim: Radicale ships no telemetry, analytics, or update-check behaviour, so no telemetry-disabling configuration is required or applied by the package.

openQuestions: No runtime network capture was performed against the pinned 3.7.1 image; conclusions rely on package configuration and upstream documentation rather than observed traffic.
CalDAV/CardDAV client apps may copy synced calendar and contact data into device or vendor cloud backups depending on each client's settings, which is outside the server package's control.
The package provisions a single bootstrap Radicale user; multi-user authentication, password rotation, and DAV auto-discovery are future package work not covered by this review.
